title: A certified local firm on the same contract team as its own recorded affiliate
question: Is any certified firm carried on a contract team, with local-business status, beside a firm that the City itself records as one whose participation it cannot be credited with?
finding: On 38 contracts, a subcontractor carrying the local-business flag works under a prime contractor or joint-venture member that the directory records as its affiliate (38 pairings, 8 distinct firm pairs, $6.4 million in listed subcontract shares). The most frequent: LAVINA TRUCKING, INC. under ESQUIVEL GRADING & PAVING INC, on 22 contracts ($5.1 million). 70 more pairings of recorded affiliates on one team are of other kinds (two subcontractors, or the certified firm as the prime).
how: Affiliations are read from the directory's "participation credit restrictions" field, in either direction (the subcontractor's entry names the prime, or the prime's entry names the subcontractor). Every contract team in the Controller's contract file is searched for a subcontractor with the local-business flag whose prime contractor or joint-venture member is such an affiliate (normalised name key, first 30 characters compared). The amount is the share the contract file assigns to the subcontractor.
limits: A restriction does not forbid two affiliates from working together; it means the certified firm's share is not supposed to count toward a goal where the affiliate is the bidder (the directory does not say which rule applies, so check the contract's own goal and the Contract Monitoring Division's crediting). The restriction list is today's: the affiliation may postdate an old contract. The contract file's local-business flag is as recorded at award. Names can match a different firm with the same name.
